name: roadmate-platform
description: Root package runner for RoadMate Platform dashboards and mobile apps
_comment_workspaces: Phase 2. `client/` and `server/` are deliberately NOT workspaces: they have their own lockfiles and node_modules and are installed with --prefix below, and hoisting two working deployments into a shared tree buys nothing. The Expo apps and the packages they share are the only things that need one dependency graph.

scripts.install:all: npm run install:client; npm run install:server
scripts._comment_sweeper: The accept window is enforced by this process, not by the API. Any environment an app is demoed against must be running it, or no 60-second timer ever expires (PLAN §1.5).
scripts._comment_business: One codebase, FOUR shipped apps (HANDOFF §4, revised 2026-08-08). `business` is an alias for the shop variant — the busiest of the four, and the usual one to have running. Six Play Store listings in total: these four plus RoadMate (customers) and RoadMate Rider.
scripts._comment_rider: Phase 3. ONE listing, unlike the four above — a shop's own delivery boy and a RoadMate delivery partner use the same app, so there is no variant to pick (HANDOFF §3).
scripts._comment_consumer: Phase 4. The sixth listing and the third codebase — one app, seven industries. Like the rider app there is no variant to pick; the industry switcher is inside the app.
scripts._comment_devbuild: Expo SDK 57 is ahead of the Expo Go published on the app stores, so Expo Go cannot open these apps at all. Build your own dev client instead — `npm run build:dev` inside apps/consumer, apps/rider or apps/business. Needs a free Expo account (`npx eas login`) and a COMMITTED working tree, because EAS uploads only what git tracks. Install the APK once; after that the `consumer`/`rider`/`shop` scripts above connect to it exactly as they did to Expo Go, and only a NATIVE dependency change needs a rebuild.
